---
title: "Fine-geometry calculator"
description: "Compute exact Gaussian-model budgets entirely in your browser."
toc: false
---

Change the dimensions below. The calculation runs locally through Pyodide;
values are not sent to a server. The first load downloads the scientific Python
runtime.

::: {.calculator}
<label for="calc-d">Ambient dimension d</label>
<input id="calc-d" type="number" min="2" value="768">
<label for="calc-m">Sketch dimension m</label>
<input id="calc-m" type="number" min="1" value="64">
<label for="calc-q">Candidate count q</label>
<input id="calc-q" type="number" min="2" value="10">
<button id="calc-run">Compute exact budget</button>
<p id="calc-status" aria-live="polite">Runtime not loaded yet.</p>
<div id="calc-result" class="metric-grid"></div>
:::

```{=html}
<script type="module">
import { loadPyodide } from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v0.27.7/full/pyodide.mjs";
const status = document.getElementById("calc-status");
status.textContent = "Loading scientific Python…";
const pyodide = await loadPyodide();
await pyodide.loadPackage(["numpy", "scipy"]);
status.textContent = "Ready.";

document.getElementById("calc-run").addEventListener("click", async () => {
  const d = Number(document.getElementById("calc-d").value);
  const m = Number(document.getElementById("calc-m").value);
  const q = Number(document.getElementById("calc-q").value);
  if (!(d > m && m > 0 && q >= 2)) {
    status.textContent = "Use integers satisfying 0 < m < d and q ≥ 2.";
    return;
  }
  status.textContent = "Computing quadrature…";
  pyodide.globals.set("d", d); pyodide.globals.set("m", m); pyodide.globals.set("q", q);
  const raw = await pyodide.runPythonAsync(`
import json, math
from scipy.integrate import quad
from scipy.special import betaln, gammaln, digamma
a, b = m/2, (d-m)/2
f = lambda x: math.asin(math.sqrt(x))*math.exp((a-1)*math.log(x)+(b-1)*math.log1p(-x)-betaln(a,b))
pair = .5 + quad(f, 0, 1, points=[0,1], limit=300)[0]/math.pi
h = lambda k: k/2+math.log(2)+gammaln(k/2)+(1-k/2)*digamma(k/2)
json.dumps({
  "HGR ceiling": math.sqrt(m/d),
  "mutual information (nats)": h(d)-h(d-m),
  "pairwise agreement": pair,
  "expected Kendall tau": 2*pair-1,
  "mean / scale information": m/d,
  "shape information": (m-1)*(m+2)/((d-1)*(d+2)),
  "nearest-neighbor chance": 1/q
})`);
  const values = JSON.parse(raw);
  document.getElementById("calc-result").innerHTML = Object.entries(values)
    .map(([label,value]) => `<div class="metric-card"><div class="value">${value.toFixed(5)}</div>${label}</div>`)
    .join("");
  status.textContent = "Exact finite-dimensional budget computed. Nearest-neighbor chance is shown; use Python for p_q.";
});
</script>
```

::: {.callout-note}
The browser calculator evaluates the exact pairwise law but deliberately does
not hide model assumptions. For the nearest-neighbor Gaussian-score kernel,
spectrum-aware quantities, batch reports, or real data, use `rpgeom` in Python.
:::
